Hi Kimberly / Grace,

Thanks for the Q1 report you shared (attached). A couple items jumped out from our operations team:
- Token spend jumped ~42% MoM in March after we rolled the new embedding pipeline.
- Average gen latency increased ~120ms on peak traffic (95th pct).

We have our internal renewal window in mid-May and need to understand if a modest commit increase (20%+) + a 12-month term makes sense. Major asks from my side: a concise ROI recap for two options (continue hosted at current rate vs. move to reserved capacity dedicated pool) and an estimated day-1 latency improvement if we opt for quantized model variants.

Can we schedule a 30m deep-dive next week? I can loop Maria (procurement) once we have rough numbers.

Attached: monthly-usage-march-2027.pdf

Best,
Jordan Fisher

Jordan — quick note ahead of the deck:

We ran an initial slice on Solvex's March traffic and produced a concise ROI summary (see linked Drive). High-level findings:
- March token mix: 58% embedding calls, 32% completion, 10% assistant/chat.
- Effective blended cost (hosted): ~$0.0019 per 1k tokens (after current discounts).
- Estimated cost for equivalent load on Dedicated (quantized 4-bit medium): ~$0.0011 per 1k tokens — ~42% unit savings before amortized infra.
- Latency: switching to a dedicated pool with KV-prefetch and optimized batching yields about 80–140ms median improvement under the March peak profile (95th improvement smaller but meaningful).

Suggested ask for your procurement team: a 12-month reserved pool with an initial 20% commit uplift and a 60-day pilot clause for performance validation. That gives both sides guardrails.

Link to working doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfGhIjKlMno

Jordan — adding a technical note from the ops side.

We simulated Solvex's March burst pattern against a dedicated pool and validated two levers that materially affect both latency and cost:
- Quantized medium model (4-bit): token cost reduction ~18% relative to hosted FP16 for completion calls while maintaining quality within your test prompts.
- Smart continuous batching with per-route slice: reduces average per-token overhead by ~12% at 95%ile throughput.

Attached is an ops runbook with measurement points and a quick checklist so your SREs can validate the pilot (ops-runbook.md). For the pilot we'll instrument the same traffic routing and KV prefetch settings to get an apples-to-apples comparison.

If you want, we can include a short SLO appendix in the amendment for Day-1 targets (latency and 99th stability).

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
